newsitem.title: GREECE: Liquidity concerns lift Greek yield curve.
newsitem.headline: Liquidity concerns lift Greek yield curve.

text.p: Greek depos and forex forwards firmed another 15 to 20 basis points across the board on forex outflows linked to uncertainty about the taxation of derivatives and interest income from treasuries, dealers said.
"The yield curve has shifted upward 15 to 20 basis points on worries about a liquidity squeeze from forex outflows related to concern about tax issues," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The Bank of Greece sold 375 million ecus to banks at the fixing and ecu/drachma firmed to 301.20 from Friday's 300.85 drachmas.
A dealer said that Salomon Brothers was the main player behind the ecu purchases.
Small amounts of $25 millon and 75 million marks were also sold by the central bank at the fixing, a dealer at a state bank said.
"As we stand, interbank liquidity depends heavily on forex developments and there is concern that continued outflows could turn the market short," a dealer at a state bank said.
Press reports said last week that the finance ministry was planning to slap a 15 percent tax on income earned on derivatives -- options, FRAs, swaps -- to help shore up budget revenues in 1997.
Other press reports said the finance ministry was going to slap a tax on interest income from T-bills effective January 1997.

The finance ministry said it would issue three-, six- and 12-month T-bills on October 31 at 12.30 percent, 11.70 percent and 11.50 percent respectively down from 12.70 percent, 12.10 percent and 11.90 percent at end-September.
The mark was quoted at 156.53/56 drachmas from Tuesday's 157.230 fix, the dollar at 238.65/75 drachmas from 237.700 and the Ecu at 300.20/25 from 301.200 drachmas.
